newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shun Tak sees shipping income drop.
newsitem.headline: Shun Tak sees shipping income drop.

text.p: Shun Tak Holdings expects income from shipping to fall about six percent in the first half of 1997, executive director Pansy Ho told Reuters on Wednesday.
Ho said the number of passengers using the company's high-speed ferry service between Hong Kong and Macau fell by about six percent in the first half of this year.
As a result, the company's shipping income should drop "more than that, but not much higher", she said.
Compared with the same period of 1996, passenger traffic fell 10-20 percent in April and May, Ho said.
The Portuguese-run enclave of Macau, about 40 km (25 miles) west of Hong Hong, has been hit by a wave of gang-related killings, bombings and other crimes in recent months.
Passenger traffic has rebounded in June to levels comparable with June 1996, Ho said.
Ho said she expects passenger volume to grow in July as more tourists come to Hong Kong. People visiting Hong Kong often travel to Macau as well.
Ho said she also expects more Hong Kong people to visit Macau.
Shun Tak's market share of passenger traffic to Macau has fallen to 68-70 percent compared with more than 70 percent last year because of increased competition, she said.
